title: Relative global complete intersections are flat
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$, and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. Suppose $S=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Then $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: Put $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ and $S=P/I$. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, regard it as a prime and contract it to $\mathfrak q\prime$ of $P$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-partial-local-flat] with $i=c$. Every index $j\in\mathrm{Fin}(c)$ satisfies $j<c$, so the initial ideal is exactly $I$. This gives flatness over $R$ of $Q=P_{\mathfrak q\prime}/IP_{\mathfrak q\prime}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], $Q$ is a localization of $S$ at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$: surjectivity of $P\to S$ identifies the image of the prime complement with this complement. In Lean use the quotient-localization instance, Ideal.map_primeCompl_comap_of_surjective and IsLocalization.algEquiv. The scalar tower $R\to S\to Q$ follows from the towers through $P$. Restrict the localization isomorphism to an $R$-linear equivalence and transport flatness by Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv. Thus $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$.

proof.text: Use the maximal-ideal module formulation of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-map-local-criterion], implemented by Mathlib Module.flat_of_isLocalized_maximal. Its intermediate algebra and module are both $S$; its localized modules are $S_{\mathfrak q}$ and its maps are the canonical $S$-linear localization maps. The preceding step verifies flatness over $R$ at each maximal ideal. This criterion directly yields Module.Flat R S, avoiding a separate passage to $R_{\mathfrak p}$. RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff gives the required flat ring map. For $S=0$ there are no maximal ideals and the same criterion applies vacuously.
